did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezekiel chapter 35 opens with the prophetic formula, “The word of the LORD came to me, saying,” indicating that the following message is the word of the LORD to the prophet.
Did you know? Ezekiel is commanded to set his face toward Mount Seir and prophesy against it. At the end of the chapter, Mount Seir is mentioned alongside all of Edom.
Did you know? The main punishment pronounced against Mount Seir is that its cities will become desolate and its travelers and passersby will be cut off, so that they will know that the LORD is God.
Did you know? The text states that the reason for the punishment is Edom’s “everlasting hatred” toward Israel, as well as its actions against the Israelites in times of distress and calamity.

Did you know? The verse contains a wordplay involving the word “blood”: “I will make you bloodshed” and “bloodshed will pursue you.” Thus, the punishment is explicitly connected with blood and bloodshed.
Did you know? The destruction is described as spreading throughout the entire land: the mountains, hills, valleys, and ravines will be filled with those slain by the sword.
Did you know? Edom is described as saying that the “two nations” and “two lands” will belong to it, but the prophecy emphasizes that the LORD is there and judges its claim.
Did you know? The LORD declares that He has heard all the insults spoken against the mountains of Israel, emphasizing that even the enemy’s words do not escape His notice.
Did you know? It is not only Edom’s actions that are judged, but also its words: “You have spoken arrogantly against me with your mouth.” The LORD says explicitly, “I have heard it.”

Did you know? The prophecy describes a complete reversal: while the whole land rejoices, Mount Seir will become desolate. Edom’s joy over the destruction of Israel’s inheritance will be replaced by its own destruction.
